chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: T-Bone Walker's health and gin and orange juice
summary: T-Bone, with ulcers, took to Ramirez's screwdrivers.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But by the time you came to Europe in '68 with T-Bone, his health was going down then, wasn't it.

He wasn't very well. I did a bad thing with him. He saw me drink a screwdriver there, and he took a liking to it. Gin and orange juice. He became attached to it. Everywhere we went he'd have to have a gin and orange juice. I don't think that helped very much.
Well, he had ulcers all his life.
I didn't even know it. At that time, you know, ...(?)... It's too bad. He had a strong body.
